name: Assertion-Evidence
summary: Each slide carries a full-sentence assertion as its title and visual evidence as its body, with no bullet lists.
references: Michael Alley, The Craft of Scientific Presentations (2003)
title_style: Assertion titles: a full-sentence claim of one or two lines, under 20 words.

sequence.purpose: Name the talk as its main claim.
Further visual evidence for the assertion.

pitfalls: Sneaking bullet lists back in as evidence.
Visuals that do not prove the assertion above them.

example.topic: A fictional agricultural research team presenting greenhouse results
outline: Cooler nights explain most of the yield gain in our trial
Three findings from the two-year greenhouse trial
Yield rose fastest in beds with the lowest night temperature
Night temperature tracks yield better than light or water
Cooling at night is the cheapest lever for yield
Three findings point to night cooling
